summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of asthma, diastolic heart failure, interstitial lung disease, polymyositis, morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and chronic anticoagulation for recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for a one-week history of shortness of breath, productive cough, and chest tightness. She was not hypoxic and showed signs of an asthma exacerbation and mild heart failure flare-up. She was treated with duonebs, intravenous steroids, and a course of oral prednisone with a taper plan. IV furosemide was given for fluid overload, though kidney function was monitored due to a rise in creatinine. Her INR was subtherapeutic on admission due to missed warfarin doses; she was bridged with Lovenox and reached a therapeutic INR by discharge. Her chronic conditions remained stable, and she subjectively improved. She was discharged home on a prednisone taper, home medications, and instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and pulmonologist.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Body mass index [BMI] 70 or greater, adult
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
